deep_dive_html:
The Perils of Unregulated CAM in Industrial Leases

In manufacturing and heavy industrial leases, Common Area Maintenance (CAM) clauses are frequently weaponized to disguise capital expenditures as routine operating expenses. Landlords often exploit the ambiguity of "operating expenses" to pass through the costs of heavy-duty paving, structural repairs to loading docks, and expanded security systems—costs that should be amortized over the life of the asset rather than charged to the tenant in a single fiscal year.

Furthermore, without a clear distinction between controllable and non-controllable expenses, tenants are vulnerable to arbitrary increases in administrative fees, management markups, and landscaping overhauls. For a manufacturing entity, these unmanaged spikes can devastate predictable operational margins and disrupt long-term budgeting.

Establishing Market-Standard Protections

To protect your bottom line, your lease must include a rigorous, narrow definition of what constitutes a reimbursable expense. Effective negotiation requires the following safeguards:

  • Implement a hard cap on "controllable" expenses, such as landscaping, cleaning, and security, to prevent year-over-year volatility.
  • Explicitly exclude capital expenditures, ensuring that any necessary structural improvements are amortized over their useful life and only charged to the tenant to the extent actually incurred during the lease term.
  • Secure comprehensive audit rights, allowing the tenant to inspect landlord books and records to verify the accuracy of annual CAM reconciliations.
